plan.title: Aldosterone kidney DE and TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks which transcription factors drive the aldosterone-vs-vehicle response in human kidney (12 samples: 6 aldosterone vs 6 vehicle, unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level Salmon counts, 12000 genes). The plan first checks sample structure with a blind VST/PCA so any outlier or unexpected grouping is caught before testing, then runs a two-group DESeq2 Wald analysis (PyDESeq2, the Python implementation) with explicit vehicle reference level, BH at alpha 0.05 and apeglm-equivalent LFC shrinkage to produce a trustworthy gene-level contrast statistic. That statistic feeds transcription-factor activity inference with decoupler's univariate linear model on the CollecTRI signed regulons (primary) and DoRothEA A-C (robustness alternative), because with 12 samples no data-driven network inference is possible — a prior knowledge network is the only sound regulon source at this size. The TF activity is computed per sample on a log-scale matrix and tested aldosterone-vs-vehicle with a linear model on the scores, BH-adjusted across regulators. All scripts are Python per the user constraint; the only R artefact (the DoRothEA .rda) is read from Python via rpy2. Known limitation carried into the report: the counts are a gene-level Salmon table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so the transcript-length correction is lost and isoform-level changes can surface as gene-level DE.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
